findings.claim_in_draft: **P4.1.** Every operation in the theory's dependence order (section 6's table) is assigned to exactly one holder or to "no home".

Section 4's "phase 1 does not attribute them" covers Deploy, (G) and (EK) as attributions to agents; it does not assign them a holder or a "no home", and it says nothing about (O), (R), (N) or (U1)–(U3). findings.forced_edit: Add a row for each of (O), (R), Deploy, (N), (G), (EK) and (U1)–(U3), each with a holder or "no home"; or restate P4.1 as covering only the operations the table lists, and say which it leaves out and why.

findings.where: Section 5, P3.5, read against section 5's "Same skill (file 33)"

findings.claim_in_draft: "**M8.** A harness that sets what the model's components assign deletes those components; one that sets what they read does not." ... "*Would count against it:* the partition arm (d) of phase 3 matching arm (a) on the same-explanation verdicts and the pulling pairs"
findings.finding: No arm of phase 3 sets what the model's components assign. Arms (a) to (d) differ only in what each call is handed to read: a transcript, a summary, a document plus one test. So phase 3 tests only M8's third limb (partitioning loses shared constraints) and leaves M8's answer to Q1 — the claim about setting tokens and attention — with no test in this programme. Section 10 concedes the observation is not in the record, but the draft still puts M8 forward as the model's answer to Q1 with a phase-3 falsifier. Provenance: built from the theory, asserted as to the harness.
findings.evidence: The draft's arms: "**(a)** one Claude Code agent (Sonnet 5) carrying its own history ...; **(b)** fresh calls, one per step, each handed the whole transcript so far; **(c)** fresh calls ... each handed a summary ...; **(d)** the partition harness: fresh calls, one per test of Step 5, each handed only the document, the frozen question and the one test". Section 10: "**The owner's harness observation is claimed, not in the record.** Phase 2 asks for the material; until it comes, M8's answer to Q1 rests on the theory alone."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I read the four arms and the rig's two runners looking for any arm or any program that sets a token, a logit or an attention weight. `run.py` sends messages and reads a reply; `sonnet_agent.py` writes a prompt file and wraps a reply. Nothing in either reaches a port the model assigns.
findings.forced_edit: Split M8 in two and mark them apart: the partition claim, which arm (d) tests, and the port-setting claim, which nothing in phases 1 to 5 tests and which is left unknown with the test that would settle it named.

findings.claim_in_draft: "a deterministic harness that sets tokens or attention sets ports that the selected transport's own components assign"
findings.finding: Which ports the model's components assign is \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\) of the transformer, which section 1 puts outside the programme and hands to the physical module. M8's answer to Q1 therefore rests on a fact the programme declares itself unable to supply, and section 10's "the grain is text" does not cover it. This is a borrowed part and is not named as one. Provenance: borrowed from the physical module.
findings.evidence: Draft, section 1: "Not asked: what a transformer computes at the grain of its weights. File 10 puts that outside the semantics: \"The one thing (R) takes from outside is \\(\\operatorname{Org}_\\ell(o)\\): which organization a physical occurrence instantiates at a grain. That is supplied by the physical module, not by the semantics.\"" Draft, M1: "What organization the execution instantiates, \\(\\operatorname{Org}_\\ell\\), is the physical module's and is not claimed here."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a sentence in M8 or section 10 acknowledging that the port-assignment claim needs \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\). M1 makes the disclaimer and M8 does not carry it; section 10's grain paragraph says only that a claim at that grain "could contradict this model without the model noticing", not that M8 rests on one.
findings.forced_edit: Mark M8 borrowed from the physical module, name the module as the explanation it rests on, and say that the programme cannot settle it.

findings.claim_in_draft: "each such edit replaces a component with the full relation, and the shared constraints those components carried go with them"
findings.finding: Part II gives two different clauses and M8 fuses them. A deleted component imposes the full relation; an edit that sets a port replaces the component assigning it. Setting a port does not leave that port unconstrained — it fixes it. What goes free is the rest of the replaced component's footprint, which is the point M8 needs and is not what it says. Two readings, one of them wrong. Provenance: built, worded loosely.
findings.evidence: File 10, Part II: "A deleted component imposes the full relation on its ports. An edit that sets a port replaces the component assigning that port; it does not add an equation beside an incompatible one."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I read Part II's paragraph in full and checked whether any other sentence of file 10 says that a setting edit imposes the full relation. None does; the full-relation clause belongs to deletion alone.
findings.forced_edit: Reword: a setting edit replaces the component, so the set port is fixed and the other ports of that component's footprint lose the relation it imposed on them; that loss is what the harness costs.

findings.where: Section 4, M3, and section 3's "Why phase 3 is the first test"
findings.claim_in_draft: "Nothing about what an agent instantiates is read off one report; it is read off what changes between reports under admitted changes."
findings.finding: Derivation 9 says nothing about "one" report. It says no function of the input–output projection agrees with an account claim on two models that share the projection. What changes between reports as the input is changed is itself a function of the input–output projection, so the derivation bites on phase 3's design exactly as it bites on a single report. The word "one" is doing work the theorem does not license, and file 10 says elsewhere that fidelity is over component structure, not outputs. Provenance: built on a quotation read wider than written.
findings.evidence: File 10, Derivation 9: "If \\(M_0,M_1\\) have the same input–output projection and differ on an account claim, no function of the projection agrees with the claim on both. *Proof.* Equal inputs to a function give equal outputs. ∎ ... The same holds for attribution from emitted text and for use inferred from delivery logs." File 10, Part 0: "Fidelity in this semantics is over **component structure under change**, not over outputs. Two systems with identical outputs and different internal routes are different organizations here, and the semantics says so." File 33, SKILL.md: "**Look inside.** Matching the results is not matching the workings. Two machines can give the same outputs by different routes. ... use changes that reach inside."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I read Derivation 9 in full and searched file 10 for any sentence limiting it to a single observation or licensing multi-observation inference. There is none; the proof is one line about functions of a projection.
findings.forced_edit: Say what phase 3 can settle: it separates *arrangements* by their projections; it does not settle what any arrangement instantiates. Mark the instantiation claims of M4, M5 and M6 unknown at this grain, with "look inside" named as the test that cannot bite.

findings.claim_in_draft: "A stateful agent is one whose executions return into a state that carries the represented targets of its unfinished work (the retention fixed point, CT2)"
findings.finding: CT2 says nothing about represented targets or unfinished work. It is a monotone fixed point over states whose executions complete and return into C. The clause "carries the represented targets of its unfinished work" is the draft's own addition, built from Part IV's constructed-transport condition, and is not marked as a construction although the draft's own rule in section 0 requires marking. Provenance: built, unmarked.
findings.evidence: File 10, Part XII: "**Retention fixed point.** \\(F(C)\\) = states whose executions all complete and return into \\(C\\). \\(F\\) is monotone; \\(C\\subseteq F(C)\\) is the invariant form; the union of post-fixed sets is the greatest fixed point. (CT2)" Draft, section 0: "where the plan builds something the theory permits but does not contain, it says so."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I searched file 10 for "represented target" and found it only at Part IV line 212; Part XII's CT1, CT2, Can and CanAdv contain no occurrence of it. I also checked whether M5's later quotation of Owned capability supplies it: it does not.
findings.forced_edit: Mark the clause a construction, name Part IV's "available as a represented target" and Part XII's CT2 as the two passages it is built from, and say that file 10 does not join them.

findings.claim_in_draft: "And Part X's construction needs \"an actual subhistory owned by \\(s\\)\" in which the target is \"available as a represented target\"."
findings.finding: The second quotation is Part IV's, not Part X's. M6 attributes the same words to Part IV correctly; M5 does not. A misplaced Part number is the same family of fault the H69 word-list check corrected twice. Provenance: asserted.
findings.evidence: File 10, Part IV, "Constructed": "There is an episode (Part X) whose construction witness prepares \\(t\\), and in which \\(t\\), or the organization it targets, is available as a represented target." Part X's Build reads: "holds when an actual subhistory owned by \\(s\\) and delimited at \\(e\\) prepares a represented organization for explanatory use of \\(c\\), contains a nontrivial binding construction relevant to that use, and is not a composition of content-preserving transfers." Draft, M6: "Part IV: a constructed transport needs an episode \"in which \\(t\\), or the organization it targets, is available as a represented target\"".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I searched file 10 for the string "available as a represented target": one hit, line 212, in Part IV. Part X contains no such phrase.
findings.forced_edit: Attribute the phrase to Part IV, as M6 does.

findings.claim_in_draft: "The record of this repository is such a memory: \"A history \\(h\\) is a set of occurrences with an acyclic causal precedence \\(\\prec_h\\)\" (Part IX)"
findings.finding: The quotation is cut at a comma with no ellipsis, and the omitted clause is a third requirement of the definition. M7's falsifier list then names only the two requirements the truncated quote carries, so the test cannot reach the clause the definition actually imposes. This is the fault the draft names as the one it is most likely to carry (section 0) and which M10's own falsifier invites. Provenance: asserted.
findings.evidence: File 10, Part IX: "A history \\(h\\) is a set of occurrences with an acyclic causal precedence \\(\\prec_h\\) and a physical interpretation supplying process occurrences, their ports, and the connections actually instantiated." Provenance: asserted.

findings.claim_in_draft: "The theory gives the reason in its own dependence order (Part XIV): what a skill is for is one of the theory's operations ... and which of those an agent can carry at one call is exactly what the model says."

Worse, read as an order of work — which is how the draft uses it — Part XIV points the other way: (O), (Q), (K), (F1), (F2), (A), (E), (S), (B), (D) come before (R), Deploy and the retention predicates, and those earlier items are the skill map's rows while (R) and retention are the model's M4 and M5. The cited passage favours map-before-model. Provenance: asserted.
findings.evidence: File 10, Part XIV: "(O) and (Q) depend on nothing. ... (E) depends on those. (S), (B), (D) depend on (E). (R) depends on (F1)–(F2) and physical provenance. ... Deploy depends on (R) and (CT1)." Section 6's table gives (Q), (E) and (S)(B)(D) to HV file 33 and Planning file 2; M4 is (R) and M5 is (CT1), (CT2), Can.

findings.forced_edit: Drop the claim that the theory gives the reason. Say that the reason is the writer's — the map assigns operations and cannot assign them without knowing which an agent can carry at a call — and note that Part XIV's order, read as work, favours the owner's order.

findings.claim_in_draft: "**Q1.** \"creating a determinist harness that serves as an attention and token distribution system is difficult to implement without destroying the already latent LLM capabilities.\" Why, in the theory's terms, and which harnesses would not."

findings.where: Section 5, P1.2, P1.3, P1.4, against section 13 and file 33

findings.claim_in_draft: "**(b)** fresh calls, one per step, each handed the whole transcript so far; **(c)** fresh calls, one per step, each handed a summary of the transcript written by a fixed program; **(d)** the partition harness ... Same skill (file 33), same documents, same framing."

Arm (a) is the nearest thing that exists and even it needs `JOBS` and the manifest changed. Provenance: asserted.

It carries Claude Code's own system prompt and has tools. The plans' reader had only the framing text and the document."

findings.claim_in_draft: "Checking an account: (F1), (F2), (A), non-circular, non-vacuous (Part V) | (E) | HV file 33, Step 5 | none named"

verdict:
**1. The question, frozen.** What is being explained: whether this draft research plan answers the owner's note H6 sentence by sentence, and whether its phase 3 can be run and marked with what the repository holds. Range: the draft as written, file 10 as the authority, and the record of the four projects. What is asked: which parts of the draft are held, by what, and what would count against each — a judgment of the plan, not of the theory and not a forecast of whether the programme will succeed. The question kind is mixed: "does it achieve its purpose?" for the plan's answers to H6, and "what can we tell from what we see?" for whether phase 3 can be run. Frozen for this report; anything I found that would change it is recorded as a new claim, not folded back in.

**2. The explanation in parts, and the jobs.** The draft's parts in its own words: M1 to M10 (the model sketch), section 6's thirteen-row skill map, P1.1 to P4.2 (the predictions), the five-phase order, and the rules in sections 2, 7 and 8. The jobs, tagged: **given** — answer H6's sixteen sentences, and in particular the six unknowns Q1 to Q6 as the draft numbers them (the owner named these); **fixed** — the theory is file 10 and only file 10, the two skills are frozen, the other projects are read only, nothing runs before the owner's word (the owner put these outside the test, decisions S4, H6, H7, H8); **added** — everything I tested in section 6 and section 5 against the record's own programs and results, which is my job list, not the owner's, and parts held only by it are held only relative to it.

**3. Part by part.** M1 *fixed*, declared by the owner of the draft and said so, provenance declared by its author. M2 *loose*, provenance asserted: two of the four clauses are asserted rather than shown. M3 *contradicts*, provenance built: its licence is wider than Derivation 9's words, and the same theorem bites on phase 3's design. M4 *held*, provenance built: its quotations of (R), Part X's relay clause and Part IV's carrier clause are exact and its falsifier is a run this repository can make. M5 *construction* on the retention clause and *contradicts* on the Part X attribution, otherwise *held if* — held only by phase 3, which cannot run yet. M6 *held if*, held by P3.4, which rests on an audit H61 says cannot be enforced. M7 *contradicts* on the truncated Part IX definition; the rest *held*. M8 split: the partition limb *held if* (arm d), the port-setting limb *unknown* (no arm tests it) and *borrowed* from the physical module. M9 *held if* on representation and *idle* in its last sentence. M10 *held* on six of seven mappings, all quoted exactly; *contradicts* on the history mapping through M7's truncation. Section 6's table: *contradicts* on completeness (nine operations left out), on double assignment (the contract twice), on three rows carrying a holder and "no home" at once, on row 5's (K1) gap, on row 12's "one component", on row 9's "no home", and *loose* on rows 2 and 11. P1.4 and P1.2 *contradict* file 33's no-counting rule and the draft's own trap. P3.1 *held if*, on marker reliability H64 shows is absent for swap and poke. P3.2 and P3.3 *contradict* H64's strike of the same-explanation count. P3.4 *held if*. P3.5 *contradicts* twice: the run count and the change of authority file. P4.1 *contradicts* the table it points at. The five-phase order *two routes*: two readings of H6 and the draft names one. Every mark's provenance sits beside it in the findings.

**4. Whole-explanation checks, by their Step 5 names.** **Remove**: removing M8's port-setting limb costs phase 3 nothing, because no arm reaches it — that is how I found the limb is unheld. Removing M9's last sentence costs nothing. **Swap**: swapping "two documents" for "two runs" in P3.1 changes the threshold and the draft itself does both, which shows the unit is loose. Swapping "same-explanation verdicts" for "pulling pairs" in P3.2 leaves the prediction reading identically, which shows the three cross-step fields are one field for the plan's purposes and are not separately held. **Flip the outcome**: section 8 covers both directions for P3.1, P3.2, P3.3, P3.4, P4.1 and P4.2, which is the right answer; P1.1's two outcomes both lead to a change and neither ends the programme, which is a patch made in advance. **Poke**: I changed one thing the draft says should matter (which authority file the readers get) and P3.5's ground moved; I changed one it says should not (which of two rig runners sends arm a) and nothing in the predictions moved, which is the honest pair. **Reverse**: could not bite. There are no results yet to poke at the effect end; the draft's own sentence that leaves it nothing to reach is "Nothing in this plan runs before the owner's word on that phase." M5, M6 and M8 as causal claims are left *unknown* with Reverse named. **Hunt the answer in the starting points**: it bites, and it finds one — section 3 puts the phase order into Part XIV and then reads it back out, where Part XIV supplies only a list. **Add a job**: I added "the plan must say what would show a workflow embodies the theory" and the draft does not survive it unchanged; that job rules out every version of phase 5 the draft now permits. **Build the best rival**: the rival is map-before-model, the owner's stated order; nothing on the draft's change list separates the two before phase 4, and Part XIV read as work favours the rival. **Pull**: Planning file 2's "every prediction names the count that would falsify it" pulls against file 33's "do not count confirmations, jobs or parts"; P1.4 is where it gives way, and the draft does not name the pair. **Check the patches**: the record's zero-CANNOT count is carried into P3.5 across a change to the thing under test; the reserve is carried from splits.md without H69's caution. **Look inside**: could not bite. The draft's own sentence that leaves it nothing to reach is "**The grain is text.** \\(\\operatorname{Org}_\\ell\\) of a transformer is outside the programme by choice (section 1)." M1, M2 and M8's port claim are left *unknown* with Look inside named. What the change list leaves out: any change reaching inside a model, and any arm that sets what a model assigns.

**5. What would make it harder to vary.** Two things, in order. First, write phase 3's marking plan as its own frozen file before anything else: define the three new fields, run the third reading H63 and Planning file 2 both require, and set the per-field tolerance from H64's recorded inter-marker disagreement rather than from one number. Without that, P3.1, P3.2 and P3.3 cannot bite. Second, split M8 in two and mark the port-setting limb unknown, naming the harness that would settle it; that is the owner's Q1, and as the plan stands nothing in phases 1 to 5 reaches it.

**6. What this does not show.** Nothing here says the model is wrong, that the owner's harness observation is wrong, or that phase 3 will fail. A loose part may be true. I have not shown that any arrangement of an LLM does or does not instantiate any of the theory's objects, and I could not: the change list of this judgment is a set of documents, and every test that needs a run was left unknown with its name attached. Hard to vary is not true.

**7. One next step.** Before phase 1, write the phase 3 marking plan and run the third reading on the fields H64 struck — because if those fields cannot carry a claim, P3.1 to P3.3 are the plan's only load-bearing falsifiers and the programme has none.
